The reported joins use already validated roots/names.
findings.residual_owner_action: No defect found in these locations. Upstream owner should preserve the segment, root-containment, relative-path, and same-origin checks if this flow changes.

findings.reachable_path_and_inputs: The core read/list path may be used by a runtime tool, but the listed item name comes from the directory iterator and is canonicalized; the relevant path does not bypass root containment.
findings.justification: Directory listing starts from a real path, resolves each child through fs.realPath, and rejects entries whose resolved target is outside the listing root. Symlink escapes are filtered before an entry is returned.
findings.residual_owner_action: No defect found. Keep realpath containment and add regression coverage if listing semantics change.

findings.reachable_path_and_inputs: The helper is used for glob/permission matching. Its rules are control-plane/config inputs, not arbitrary task text in the AIAT adapter. The reported dynamic RegExp is intentional glob implementation.
findings.justification: The function escapes regular-expression metacharacters in the pattern before translating only glob wildcards (* and ?) into regex operators. The pattern is not inserted as raw regular-expression syntax.
findings.residual_owner_action: No injection defect found. Upstream owner may bound pattern length if permission/config inputs ever become untrusted or denial-of-service risk is demonstrated.

findings.reachable_path_and_inputs: The scanned upstream Dockerfile is not the Dockerfile used for the AIAT service image; AIAT deployment controls the image recipe and runtime user.

findings.reachable_path_and_inputs: This is the package CLI launcher, not an AIAT task-controlled shell invocation. Executable selection is reviewed separately in records 128–129.
findings.justification: The wrapper calls child_process.spawn(target, process.argv.slice(2)) without shell:true or a shell command string. Arguments remain an argv array; the rule flags generic child-process use.
findings.residual_owner_action: No shell-injection defect. Keep executable identity and package-path controls separate from argv handling.

findings.reachable_path_and_inputs: This is startup-time package launcher code. In the AIAT profile the image/package tree is pinned and root-owned, the process runs as UID 10001, and the runtime environment is explicitly configured; no worker task input selects these paths. A deployment that forwards OPENCODE_BIN_PATH or makes searched parents writable would change that assessment.
findings.justification: The launcher can select an executable from OPENCODE_BIN_PATH, a cached binary, or package directories found by walking ancestors. The argv launch itself is shell-free, but executable identity depends on environment/package-tree trust.
findings.residual_owner_action: Upstream launcher maintainers should validate the override and constrain searched paths/ownership. AIAT deployment owner should keep OPENCODE_BIN_PATH unset and the package tree immutable; re-review any change to environment propagation.

findings.reachable_path_and_inputs: The finding is reachable only through the upstream CLI agent-create command, not through AIAT WorkerRun: AIAT submits task text to the HTTP prompt_async endpoint and denies native tools. This is still a real upstream CLI trust-boundary issue.
